identity.name: Lange 1

case.bezel: polished pink gold, integrated with case, no separate ring

identity.one_liner: The decentralized dial layout that relaunched German watchmaking in 1994, still built around the outsize date it made standard across the industry.

provenance_events.description: Walter Lange presents the Lange 1 in Dresden on 24 October 1994, four years after German reunification. The watch — with its off-centre dial, outsize date, and the first in-house movement from the re-founded A. Lange & Söhne — defines the modern German haute horlogerie school.

narrative.story: The Lange 1 was one of four watches shown at the October 1994 Dresden press conference that marked A. Lange & Söhne's re-entry into watchmaking after the East German state had absorbed the original firm in 1948. Its off-center dial, with hours and minutes pushed to the left and a matching outsize date at 12 o'clock, broke from the round-and-centered layout every other manufacture used at the time. The outsize date shown here, assembled from two overlapping discs instead of a single ring, became a specification other brands later copied outright.
narrative.collector_notes: Case metal and dial color define the value spread across Lange 1 references; this pink gold, argenté-dial 191.032 sits in the middle of the range. Collectors check for even patina on the solid silver dial and confirm the power-reserve indicator at 3 o'clock reads full when fully wound, since the underlying L121.1 is hand-wound and a lazy reserve display is often the first sign of service need.
